issues.source_quote: А и Б играли на трубе!
issues.translation_quote: Little Boy Blue, come blow your horn!
issues.justification: The reference is to the Soviet children's riddle 'А и Б сидели на трубе'; the translator swaps in an English nursery rhyme, which changes the allusion to a different one with no connection to the original wordplay on 'труба'.

issues.source_quote: Три храбреца, три храбреца в одном тазу, в одном тазу пустились по морю в грозу..
issues.translation_quote: Three wise men, three wise men of Gotham, in a bowl, in a bowl, went to sea in a storm...
issues.justification: Source says 'храбрецы' (brave men), not 'wise men'; 'of Gotham' is an addition. Partial domestication creates an inconsistency with the Russian text and is not signaled.

issues.source_quote: Довели об этом до вашего сведения... Горько, горько!
issues.justification: 'Горько!' is a Russian wedding chant demanding the couple kiss; Ogurtsov's follow-up pun ('Горько, товарищи, чувствовать, что мы стали на год старше') relies on it. 'Bitter it is, comrades' is nonsensical without explanation and the pun/joke fails; adding 'Kiss!' also is an unsupported addition.

issues.source_quote: Ансамбль пенсии и пляски! Виноват, простите, ансамль Песни и пляски!
issues.translation_quote: The Pension and Dance Ensemble! My mistake, sorry, the Song and Dance Ensemble!
issues.justification: The Freudian slip 'песни'→'пенсии' is a pun that depends on phonetic similarity; 'Pension' vs 'Song' loses it entirely in English.

issues.translation_quote: To Cucumber? Thank you so much
issues.justification: Ogurets/Ogurtsov wordplay: the old man mangles the name into a diminutive 'Огурец'. Rendering as 'Cucumber' without a name-mangling signal in English reads oddly, and the comedic mispronunciation of surnames (Frolova/Krylova) is lost in flow; also inconsistent with elsewhere using 'Ogurtsov'.

issues.source_quote: Здрасте, тётя Дуся!... Усиков... Огурцов... серым веществом головного мозга
issues.justification: 'Коты в Сапогах' rendered as 'Pusses in Boots' is an odd, unnatural plural; the joke (cut the cats, no money for boots) is muddled.

issues.translation_quote: Sleight of hand, and no speech!
issues.justification: Acceptable literal, but the earlier 'И доклад у него в кармане!' (the speech is in his pocket / sleight of hand with a bird) pun is flattened, losing the double meaning.

issues.source_quote: Снизу звёздочки кажутся маленькие-маленькие. ... две звёздочки, три звёздочки.. Четыре звёздочки, лучше всего, конечно, пять звёздочек!
issues.translation_quote: two-star, three-star... Four-star, and best of all, of course, five-star!
issues.justification: The lecturer is drunk and drifts into cognac star ratings; the translation keeps this but does not convey the hotel/cognac joke any better, and 'Assa... Assa...' remains untranslated gibberish; acceptable but the humor is weak. Borderline.

Source deliberately mispronounces 'серьёзно' as Ogurtsov's idiolect; the English uses a misspelling 'serrious' that is hard to read and is used inconsistently, and may appear as typos rather than character voice.

issues.translation_quote: That's three cubic meters of planks.
issues.justification: Reasonable, but 'на то' is dropped; minor nuance.
'Кручина' (grief/sorrow) pun in composer's name is lost, though it supports the 'very mournful music' gag.

issues.translation_quote: They're making a Punch-and-Judy clown out of the director, you see?!
issues.justification: 'Петрушка' is a Russian puppet fool; 'Punch-and-Judy clown' is clumsy and 'понимаешь' is mistranslated as 'you see' in a way that loses Ogurtsov's tic.

Fine, but earlier 'Значит, по вашему... раз в экономистами кидаться' 'throwing economists around' is rendered literally without clarifying that the economist is a person on stage being tossed, leaving the joke obscure.
Literal rendering of 'зубастая' (biting, satirical) is unnatural in English; 'sharp' or 'biting' would work better.

issues.source_quote: Вы, собственно, соображаете, что вы делате?!
issues.translation_quote: Do you actually realize what you're doing?!
issues.justification: Loses the bureaucratic, scolding sneer of 'собственно'; adequate but flat.

issues.source_quote: Больше ничего известный- неизвестный не сказал?
issues.translation_quote: And the known stranger didn't say anything else?
issues.justification: The oxymoron 'известный-неизвестный' is a playful phrase ('the famous unknown'); 'known stranger' is awkward.

issues.source_quote: Секретаря дирекции, Тосю Бурыкину / Тосю Буракину
issues.justification: Source has the name inconsistently written; translation silently normalizes. Also 'Frolova' mix-up is fine. Low impact.

issues.translation_quote: Attention, comrades, friends! No one may be bored at our party!
issues.justification: 'Скучать нельзя' rendered as 'No one may be bored' is stilted; a more natural slogan-like English would suit the festive verse.
